title: Streamline variant journeys and auto-layout hierarchy for tokens, buttons, tables, charts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Reduce accidental visual regressions and speed up component consumption by reorganizing variant sets, normalizing auto-layout hierarchies, and enforcing a predictable naming taxonomy. This ticket covers tokens to component mapping, button and table row variants, chart legend and axis components, and a publish gating checklist for the Figma library. Outcomes: 1) Single source variant patterns for interactive states (hover/focus/pressed/disabled) 2) Auto-layout frames normalized to explicit axis direction + padding tokens 3) Naming scheme for components and variant values that maps to code tokens and props 4) A publish checklist and rollback plan to avoid breaking downstream consumers.
comments: 2026-02-18 Maya Chen: Scoped initial audit across components. Found three distinct problems: (A) variant sets with mixed semantic/value names (e.g., 'primary/1/hover'), (B) nested auto-layout frames using mixed axis (row in a column) causing shrink-wrap regressions, (C) token aliasing where spacing tokens differ from CSS variables. Proposal: canonicalize variant naming to <role>/<state> (e.g., button/primary/hover), flatten instance inheritance for atoms, convert spacing to token-based frame padding.

2026-02-23 Arjun Patel (Engineering): Reviewed proposal — engineering prefers variant keys that match props in React components (appearance + state). Agreed on <appearance> and <state> but raised concern about migration impact for existing instances in product repos. Suggested add linting rule and codemod in parallel to Figma changes.

2026-02-27 Maya Chen: Performed targeted refactor on Buttons and Table rows in the draft library file. Created mapping sheet in Confluence linking old component names to new names and listing instances likely to be affected. Added an 'instance-migration' tab with screenshots for the partner squads.

2026-03-02 UX Review (Tina Alvarez): Approved visual decisions for compact and default density. Requested that accessible focus rings remain purely token-driven and called out in component specs. Action: add explicit focus token mapping and keyboard guidance in the component notes.

2026-03-05 Eng Follow-up (Priya Singh): Implementing a codemod to rename props and to detect deprecated instance names. Engineering will add an integration test to the Visual Regression pipeline to compare pre/post snapshots for the set of high-risk components (buttons, primary table, chart legend).

2026-03-09 Maya Chen: Began auto-layout cleanup sweep. Replaced nested mixed-axis groups in 42 components; switched to explicit horizontal/vertical frames and normalized padding to tokens: spacing.xs/spacing.md/spacing.lg. Flagged 6 complex chart atoms (axis group) for deeper investigation — they use absolute positioning for tick labels which will block auto-layout normalization.

2026-03-11 PM Review (Liam O'Connor): Good progress. Request: for the publish window, schedule a short deprecation notice to Design System slack and create a migration playbook for mobile teams. Also requested that we keep a rollback branch of the library file until two release cycles pass.

2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Locked draft for final QA. Next steps: (1) complete chart axis normalization (owner: Maya), (2) land codemod PR and run across feature branches (owner: Priya), (3) publish gating: staged publish, notify integrators, keep rollback branch for 2 weeks post-publish.
2026-03-12 Maya Chen: QA checklist added as comment. Will run visual diff for these pages: Buttons (primary/secondary/ghost), Tables (row-density variants), Charts (legend + axes).

notes: Trade-offs: we will temporarily increase the number of component instances that need migration to gain long-term consistency. For complex chart atoms we may accept a smaller subset of auto-layout normalization and ship a focused follow-up to replace absolute-positioned tick layout. Aim is to minimize runtime risk while delivering predictable tokens/variants for devs.
